title: CSS Animations
definition: The `animation` property is a shorthand for eight individual animation properties (name, duration, timing-function, delay, iteration-count, direction, fill-mode, and play-state).
simpleExplanation: Once you write a `@keyframes` script, you use the `animation` property as the 'Play Button'. You can tell the browser to play it fast, play it in reverse, delay the start by 5 seconds, or play it on an infinite loop.
realWorldExample: A success checkmark that scales up and pops into existence exactly 0.5 seconds after a modal opens (`animation-delay: 0.5s;`).

answers.question: Infinite?
answers.answer: It makes the animation repeat forever (perfect for loading spinners).

answers.question: Fill mode forwards?
answers.answer: By default, when an animation finishes 100%, the element snaps back to its original 0% state. `forwards` tells the element: 'When the animation is done, freeze in place at the 100% state'.
